answer: Under NIST SP 800-63B-4: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL require passwords used as a single-factor authentication mechanism to be a minimum of 15 characters in length. Verifiers and CSPs MAY allow passwords only used as part of multi-factor authentication processes to be shorter but SHALL require them to be a minimum of eight characters in length. Verifiers and CSPs SHOULD permit a maximum password length of at least 64 characters.

objections: The answer claims verifiers SHALL permit secrets at least 64 characters while the cited NIST passage states Verifiers and CSPs SHOULD permit a maximum password length of at least 64 characters.
The csrc.nist.gov final landing-page citation is claimed to support the 64-character sentence but verification shows it contains only title and abstract text.
The answer narrows the 8-character rule to as a second factor while NIST states only used as part of multi-factor authentication processes with a minimum of eight characters.
